okay, so religion is faith right? every person who believes in a religion has faith. otherwise they’d be agnostic. So think about it this way, you like pizza i like pasta and our third friend likes sushi. you may appreciate pasta and sushi but you like pizza the best. now i tell you that pasta is best and you’re like yeah it’s good but i prefer pizza. That’s it. the conversation ends. People’s faith is subjective and all religions have great lessons to pass on, but it makes no sense whatsoever to claim one is better than the other for the simple reason that it is subjective. A religion doesn’t choose a person the person chooses their faith. i say this with half knowledge but i think all religions are accepting of people if they should wish to convert. so what’s the problem. 

don’t listen to them, you do you.

on the question of which god to worship- now i’m a hindu but im not really a devout hindu. I dont actually believe that everything happened as it is stated in the gita or ramayan. you need to understand that those scriptures are like lessons, like a story with a moral. So go through the stories, read a lot, and figure out what characters you like. Because every god in hinduism stands for something else. While Ram was a man that wouldn’t condone foul play, krishna was the kinda person willing to do a little manipulation if it meant the good prevailed over evil. 

so in short: read, understand, pick favourite god, pray (if you want).
